title: Capacity Gatekeeper — Preflight sentinel for quotas, IAM, DNS, and GPU capacity checks (Private installs)
creator: Priya Patel
description:
Summary: Build a robust preflight "sentinel" (Capacity Gatekeeper) that runs as part of Private/VPC deployment pipelines to validate cloud quotas, IAM permissions, cluster DNS configuration, and GPU capacity before allowing an install or an upgrade. The goal is to convert ad-hoc manual checks into an automated, idempotent Terraform/IaC-friendly validation suite that provides clear remediation guidance and machine-readable results for CI gating.

Scope:
- Multi-cloud: AWS (EC2 quotas, ENIs, EBS limits), GCP (quotas, GPU availability, regional quotas), Azure (GPU SKUs, vCPU limits).
- Identity: Ensure service account/role binding coverage and least-privilege checks for installer principal.
- DNS: Validate VPC DNS resolution settings, private hosted zones, and DNS target reachability.
- GPU capacity: Real-time capacity probe + historical telemetry check to avoid scheduling installs into saturated regions.
- Terraform integration: A set of null_resource/locals-friendly checks or a terraform provider wrapper that returns structured pass/fail for CI.
- UX: Human-friendly failure messages and a machine-readable JSON artifact for pipeline gating.

Non-goals: deep quota increase automation (we will surface required change requests and links to cloud consoles), full remediation orchestration, or replacing cloud provider-specific quota request flows.
acceptance_criteria:
1) A reusable check suite (CLI + Terraform wrapper) that returns exit code 0 on success and non-zero on failure, and emits a JSON results artifact with per-check status and remediation hints.
2) Support for AWS, GCP, and Azure for the following checks: compute quotas, GPU SKU availability, ENI/subnet capacity (AWS), private hosted zone presence and DNS resolution, and required IAM permissions.
3) Integration test matrix in CI that runs checks against test accounts (mocked for cost) and validates failure modes.
4) Dashboardable telemetry: a CloudWatch/Stackdriver metric or internal metric exposing last preflight status per customer.
5) Documentation (Confluence) with runbook steps and example terraform module usage.
6) Security review completed with least-privilege policy snippets for installer service accounts.
implementation_notes:
Planned components: 
- preflight-cli: Go binary that queries provider APIs and emits JSON; uses provider SDKs with retries and exponential backoff.
- terraform-preflight-provider: Terraform-compatible wrapper that shells out to preflight-cli and exposes results as a 'local_file' or data resource.
- CI gating: Add a pipeline step in the private-install workflow that fails fast with annotated messages.
- Telemetry: Emit metrics to metrics.redwood.internal and include log links in artifact.

Design trade-offs considered: 
- Run-time probe vs historical telemetry: we'll do a hybrid approach—probe for basic reachability and complement with a historical API call (e.g., recent provisioning failures) to detect saturated spots.
- Aggressiveness of IAM checks: prefer read-only permission checks over requiring ability to create resources to avoid wide-scoping installer credentials.
- Provider SDK vs curl: use official SDKs for richer error codes and quota fields, but still include optional lightweight HTTP fallback for environments with trimmed SDK support.

Key implementation milestones: 
- Prototype CLI and Terraform wrapper (owner: Jonah Kim) — week 1
- Add AWS/GCP baseline checks and CI tests — week 2
- Azure checks and telemetry integration — week 3
- Docs, runbook, and security review — week 4
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for each check mocked with provider fixtures.
- Integration tests in isolated test clouds with small resource quotas (scheduled nightly).
- Failure-mode tests: simulate missing IAM permissions, exhausted quotas, DNS misconfigurations, and GPU starvation and assert clear remediation messages.
- Load tests: ensure preflight run completes under 90s for a standard region.
- Canary: enable for 10% of new private installs for 2 weeks, collect false-positive metrics before full rollout.
comments: 2025-11-03 Priya Patel: Created ticket after onboarding post-mortem where a customer hit a 0-GPU region during an upgrade. Suggested building a pre-install gate to prevent similar outages.

2025-11-05 Jonah Kim: Spike complete. Prototype CLI can query AWS Service Quotas and GCP quotas; AWS ENI checks are noisy in constrained accounts — need tighter heuristics. Planning terraform wrapper next. Link to spike notes: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1X-spike-notes

2025-11-07 Maria Gomez (SRE): Reviewed design. Suggested adding a DNS reachability probe that resolves private-hosted-zones from a VPC-attached lambda/agent to verify resolver behavior. Also flagged that Azure rate-limits require jittered retry backoff. Marked security_review_required.

2025-11-09 Jonah Kim: Implemented AWS quota checks and JSON result schema. Opening PR for review: https://github.com/redwood-inference/private-install-scripts/pull/134. Unit tests attached.
Known limitation: GCP GPU quota check currently only supports region-level quotas, not SKUs — follow-up created.
2025-11-12 Priya Patel: Product reviewed acceptance criteria and requested explicit customer-facing remediation snippets for quota increase requests per cloud provider. Added to docs.
2025-11-14 Security review (internal): Scoped installer role to read/list for core services, write only for bootstrap resources. Approved with one comment to rotate temporary credentials after run.
